title: Young Kim criticizes Newsom's leadership and calls for passage of SAVE Act - North OC Times
text:
Young Kim, a U.S. Congresswoman representing California’s 40th district since 2021, has recently used her social media platform to address issues ranging from election security to California’s fiscal management under Governor Gavin Newsom.
On February 11, 2026, Kim posted about the SAVE Act, stating: “The SAVE Act isn’t controversial. Americans from all backgrounds agree that only American citizens should vote. Democrats need to get out of the way so we can secure our elections. Pass the SAVE Act now!”
Later that day, she commented on California’s high-speed rail project and Governor Newsom’s leadership: “For anyone curious about a Newsom presidency, look no further than California’s high-speed rail. 16 years. Tens of billions spent. A budget ballooning to $135 billion. Just like his ‘high-speed’ rail, Newsom is a one-way ticket to nowhere.” This post highlighted concerns over cost overruns and delays associated with the infrastructure project.
In another tweet on February 11, Kim criticized Governor Newsom’s governance: “Stable? Reliable? Under Newsom CA is hemorrhaging taxpayer dollars & driving out businesses & workers. He needs to stop running around the world trying to get attention. It’s SAD! Do your job & fix the mess you made in California.”
Young Kim has served in Congress since defeating Gil Cisneros in 2021 and previously held office in the California State Assembly from 2014 to 2016. Born in Incheon, South Korea in 1962 and currently residing in La Habra, she earned her BBA from the University of Southern California in 1985.
